newsitem.title: USA: Lan Cargo expects Chilean growth to continue.
newsitem.headline: Lan Cargo expects Chilean growth to continue.

text.p: Cargo handled by the Chilean airlines FastAir and Lan Chile will grow about 30 percent this year, one of the the airlines' top executives told Reuters Wednesday.
"This was a very good year," Ignacio Cueto, president of Lan Chile unit Lan Cargo Group, said in an interview.
Cueto said he expects the growth to slow to about 20 percent in 1997.

The Cueto family and several other investors control FastAir, an all-cargo line and LanChile, both based in Santiago. The two field 39 aircraft. The group also owns 24.9 percent of Miami-based Florida West International Airlines.

Southbound, the two carriers haul machinery, electronics, telecommunications and mining equipment. North to the United States, they carry primarily perishables including salmon, seafood and fruit. Some of the perishables continue to Asia and Europe.

For the first nine months of 1996, Fast carried the twelfth most international cargo through Miami International Airport, hauling 32,835 tons, a 14 percent increase, and LanChile carried the 22d most, or about 11,829 tons, for a 16 percent gain, according to statistics compiled by the Dade County Aviation Department. If combined they would rank eighth largest.
